findings.claim: The assessment leaves three spec gaps unresolved but cites no file paths, registry names, or locations for any of them, so they cannot drive a plan.
findings.evidence: SPEC GAP SUMMARY states "Three registry entries point to deleted worktree or scratch paths" and "A prior compatibility/canonical drift spans ten historical phases", but the packet confirms "(no file paths cited in this artifact)" — the registry, the deleted paths, and the ten affected phases are never identified anywhere in the document.
findings.suggested_fix: Name the registry file, list the three stale project IDs/paths, and identify which historical phases carry the compatibility counter drift (or point to the backup file the migration created).

findings.claim: The constraint check declares constraints N/A even though project-level constraints exist and at least one is directly relevant to a launchd service change.
findings.evidence: "constraints.md violations: N/A — no child-specific constraint file exists" contradicts the packet's KBD Constraints, which apply "for every change from phase-codex-plugin-distribution-and-ci onward"; C-05 ("Scripts under launchd are bash 3.2 compatible") is squarely applicable to a change that repaired a launchd-supervised daemon, yet no bash-3.2 compatibility check is reported.
findings.suggested_fix: Evaluate C-01 through C-05 explicitly against the touched surface, especially C-05 for any launchd-invoked script and C-02 for the mode-0600 device key handling.

findings.claim: "test coverage: FULL" is contradicted within the same section by six ignored tests.
findings.evidence: "tests: PASS — ... kbd-runtime 74 passed with 6 operator proofs ignored" is immediately followed by "test coverage: FULL"; six ignored operator proofs mean coverage is not full and the reason for ignoring them is never given.
findings.suggested_fix: Downgrade the coverage claim or state why the 6 operator proofs are legitimately ignored (e.g., require live operator credentials) and what covers their behavior instead.

findings.claim: Goal 2 is marked MET for a "service recovery and restart fix" that the assessment itself shows was never the problem and arguably never implemented.
findings.evidence: Goal: "Implement a durable service recovery and restart fix: MET", but the assessment states "launchd supervision was healthy; the blocking symptom came from stale TCP assumptions and all-or-nothing authority startup" — i.e., no recovery/restart defect existed, and the MET verdict rests on transport/signer fixes that address a different failure mode than the goal names.
findings.suggested_fix: Restate the goal verdict to reflect what was actually fixed (transport, partial availability, signer selection) and explicitly note that the restart path needed no change, so downstream stages do not plan redundant supervision work.

findings.claim: The historical compatibility/canonical drift is deferred with no assigned owner or follow-up, despite sitting inside a parent phase named for drift cleanup.
findings.evidence: "A prior compatibility/canonical drift spans ten historical phases. The built-in migration refused to discard higher compatibility counters and created a recoverable backup; this child starts a clean successor run instead of rewriting historical evidence." No goal ID covers this decision, no gap entry says where the backup lives, and no statement returns the drift question to the parent phase "openspec-mirror-drift-cleanup".
findings.suggested_fix: Record the backup's path and explicitly hand the drift-resolution decision back to the parent phase (or a named follow-up change) so it is not silently dropped when the child exits.

findings.claim: The implementation status lists the assess artifact itself as not yet recorded while this document is the assess artifact.
findings.evidence: "KBD child workflow: PARTIAL — canonical control was repaired and the child was created at revision 7; assess/plan/execute/reflect/exit artifacts remain to be recorded."
findings.suggested_fix: Reword to "plan/execute/reflect/exit artifacts remain" or note that this assessment satisfies the assess step.
